doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Women in jazz and the business
title: Swing Shift and the erasure of women's bands
summary: They discuss the International Sweethearts and Sherrie Tucker's book Swing Shift; the Darlings of Rhythm are missing from a history of the Apollo.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah. Have you ever seen those films of the International Sweethearts — is that what it was called?
And in Sherrie Tucker’s new book, I don’t know if you’ve read that, called Swing Shift, it’s one of the best books I’ve ever read.
I think I have that book, yeah.

It’s a history of the womens’ swing bands from the 30s and 40s. I’ve never read a better researched book in my life. It’s horrifying actually how women are left out of history. I mean I’ve cited this example to a million people but there was a band called the Darlings of Rhythm, this is from Sherrie’s book, that played at the Apollo Theatre more than any other band, and it was either 1944 or 1946. And in the book, The History of the Apollo, they’re not even mentioned once as even having ever played there. Just as an example of how they were completely ignored.
